scenario_text: A fixed decoder-only language-model training stack uses P parallel input transformations whose outputs are aggregated before prediction. N is the non-embedding parameter count measured in billions, P is the number of parallel streams, and L is held-out language-model loss. This is a single concrete experimental setting, not a multi-group SLDBench reproduction. Literature anchor: the parallel scaling law of Chen et al. (2025). During evolution, retain loss scaling with N and diminishing returns in P; scientifically motivated refinements may concern aggregation overhead, routing efficiency, or saturation, not arbitrary polynomial features.
